issues.body:
`+pub mod strdist;` is a net-added `pub mod` line under a published crate's `src/**`, which is exactly the condition `scripts/gate-api-skill.py` (gate G2) blocks on. Running it locally against this diff reports:

  G2 public-api→skill: FAIL
    - crates/sparq-core/src/lib.rs
    - crates/sparq-core/src/strdist.rs

AGENTS.md states this twice ("MAINTENANCE RULE (REQUIRED)" and the "Public-API → SKILL.md maintenance rule" section) and the post-batch checklist lists G2 as the enforcing gate: when a change touches a public API (`pub` item / CLI flag / HTTP route / binding), the matching `skills/<surface>/SKILL.md` must be updated in the SAME change. No `skills/**/SKILL.md` and no crate README appear in this diff, and grep finds zero mentions of `strdist` or `edit_distance` in any markdown in the tree. This gate blocks the merge as the PR currently stands.

I could not inspect PR labels from this environment (no `gh` available), so if the `skill-not-needed` escape hatch has already been applied this is satisfied — but then the justification also needs to be in the PR body, per the gate's own message.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) add a short entry for `sparq_core::strdist::edit_distance` to `skills/sparql-query/SKILL.md` (the sparq-core surface per the map in skills/SKILL.md) and/or `crates/sparq-core/README.md`, in this same PR; or (b) apply the `skill-not-needed` label and state the justification in the PR body — e.g. "internal shared helper, deduplication only, no user-facing surface" — which is the documented escape hatch. Option (a) pairs naturally with the fix for the second issue below.
issues.title: Hard G2 public-api→skill gate fails: new `pub mod strdist` on a published crate with no SKILL.md/README updated in the same PR

issues.body:
The deleted `crates/sparq-nlq/src/constrain/distance.rs` carried an explicit rationale in its doc comment: "Kept crate-private: this is an implementation detail of dictionary suggestion ranking, shared with its property tests without widening the public API. [GPT-5.6] sq-lxw27". This PR reverses that decision — `edit_distance` is now a fully public, semver-stable item on `sparq-core`, a published crate — and the new doc comment does not say why the earlier constraint no longer applies.

That matters beyond bookkeeping: AGENTS.md's core-lean rule wants `sparq-core`'s surface kept tight, and once this is `pub` on a published crate it is an API the project must keep supporting. Cross-crate reuse genuinely does require some visibility widening, so the direction is defensible — the gap is that the trade-off is undocumented, which is what will make the next agent re-litigate it.

Note this is a rationale/documentation gap, not a correctness defect: the function is behaviorally identical to all three implementations it replaces.
issues.fix_hint: Extend the module/function doc comment with one line recording the decision, e.g. "Promoted from three crate-private copies (sparq-kb, sparq-nlq) to a shared public helper so the suggestion paths cannot drift; supersedes the earlier crate-private constraint in sq-lxw27." If keeping sparq-core's published surface minimal is the priority, an alternative is `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod strdist` — reuse across workspace crates still works while signaling it is not a supported external API. Either way, mention the choice in the PR body so it is not silently re-reversed.
issues.title: Silently reverses a documented "kept crate-private, do not widen the public API" decision without recording the new rationale

issues.body:
`edit_distance_is_symmetric` and `edit_distance_satisfies_triangle_inequality` are the only checks of the metric laws for what is now a `sparq-core` public API, and after this change they live exclusively in `crates/sparq-nlq/tests/`. Consequences:

1. `cargo test -p sparq-core` does not exercise them — confirmed: `cargo test -p sparq-core --lib strdist` runs exactly 1 test (the basics case). Anyone validating sparq-core in isolation, or bisecting a sparq-core change, gets no metric-law coverage of the function they just touched.
2. The coupling is now incidental rather than structural. Before, the `#[path = "../src/constrain/distance.rs"]` include made the dependency explicit and local. Now, if sparq-nlq is ever refactored to stop depending on this helper, the laws stop being checked for the public API with no failure and no signal.

The tests themselves are valid and non-vacuous — they pass and they exercise the real production function (verified: 6 tests pass, including both proptest cases).
issues.fix_hint: Move the two proptest cases (and the `short_string()` strategy they use) into `crates/sparq-core/src/strdist.rs` under `#[cfg(test)]`, alongside `edit_distance_basics`. sparq-core already has `proptest = "1"` in `[dev-dependencies]`, so this needs no manifest change. Leave the dictionary-repair determinism tests in sparq-nlq where they belong — only the pure metric-law properties should follow the function to its new home.
issues.title: Metric-law property tests for a sparq-core public function now live only in a downstream crate's test suite

verdict.summary: Pure code-motion refactor that consolidates three byte-identical copies of Levenshtein `edit_distance` (sparq-kb::query::nl_tool, sparq-nlq::constrain::distance, and their tests) into a new `sparq_core::strdist` module. I diffed the three deleted bodies against the new one: they are character-for-character identical, so there is NO behavioral change to suggestion ranking in either consumer. The algorithm itself is a correct two-rolling-row Levenshtein (init row 0..=b.len(), cur[0]=i+1, cur[j+1]=min(prev[j+1]+1, cur[j]+1, prev[j]+cost), swap, return prev[b.len()]); the empty-input early returns are correct and the post-swap rows are fully overwritten each iteration. char-based iteration is preserved, and the new `edit_distance("é", "e") == 1` assertion is non-vacuous: the literal is NFC U+00E9 (verified: bytes c3 a9), so a byte-oriented implementation would return 2 and the test would go red. The merged unit test in strdist.rs subsumes the assertions of all three deleted tests, and the proptest metric laws (symmetry, triangle inequality) in sparq-nlq now exercise the real production function directly instead of via a `#[path]` include — strictly better. I ran: `cargo test -p sparq-nlq --test constrain_unknown_terms` (6 passed), `-p sparq-core --lib strdist` (1 passed), `-p sparq-kb --features query --lib` (16 passed), and `cargo build -p sparq-core --no-default-features` (clean) — strdist is pure-std and unconditional, so it is sound in both feature states. Grep confirms no stale reference to the deleted `constrain/distance.rs` remains. The blocking problem is process, not logic: this adds a permanent `pub mod` / `pub fn` to a published crate, and running the repo's own `scripts/gate-api-skill.py` against this diff reports FAIL for crates/sparq-core/src/lib.rs and strdist.rs — no skills/**/SKILL.md or crate README was touched in the same change, which AGENTS.md makes a REQUIRED same-PR obligation. Nothing in the diff read as an instruction to me.
